title: India's Trade Agreements in Early 2026
text:
India and the European Union concluded negotiations on a comprehensive free trade agreement on 27 January 2026, announced at a leaders' meeting in New Delhi. The deal is expected to open markets on both sides through partial liberalisation of additional tariff lines. Conclusion of negotiations does not mean the agreement is in force, as legal scrubbing, translation and ratification remain to be completed. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the deal as creating a free trade zone of two billion people.

On 7 February 2026, India and the United States issued a joint statement announcing a framework for an interim trade agreement. Under the framework, Washington will apply a reciprocal tariff of 18 per cent on most Indian goods, replacing a combined rate of 50 per cent. An executive order rescinded a further 25 per cent duty, imposed in August 2025 over India's purchases of Russian oil, effective 7 February 2026. The order directs the Commerce Secretary to monitor Russian oil imports and recommend reinstating the duty if they resume.

India has committed to eliminate or reduce tariffs on all US industrial goods and a wide range of American food and agricultural products. It intends to buy 500 billion dollars' worth of US goods over five years, covering energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products and coking coal. Sensitive sectors, including dairy, genetically modified crops, poultry and cereals, remain protected. Both governments said further negotiations were needed to complete a broader bilateral trade agreement.

On 24 February 2026, India and the Gulf Cooperation Council signed a joint statement in New Delhi formally launching negotiations on a comprehensive and mutually beneficial free trade agreement. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal and GCC Secretary-General Jasem Albudaiwi signed the document. The talks will cover trade in goods, trade in services and digital trade, with the stated aim of removing tariff and non-tariff barriers.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the Gulf Cooperation Council located?
questions.explanation: The GCC treaty provides that the Cooperation Council has its headquarters in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

questions.q: Which Schedule to the Constitution of India contains the Union List, the State List and the Concurrent List?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution sets out the Union, State and Concurrent Lists of legislative subjects.

questions.q: Under which section of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975 may the Central Government impose anti-dumping duty on articles imported below their normal value?
questions.explanation: Section 9A of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975 empowers the Central Government, by notification, to impose anti-dumping duty where an article is imported below its normal value.

questions.assertion: Article 301 of the Constitution of India guarantees freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India.
questions.reason: Article 301 was borrowed from the commerce clause of the Constitution of the United States.
questions.explanation: Article 301 is true as a statement of the guarantee, but it was derived from Section 92 of the Australian Constitution, not from the US Constitution.

statements: I. Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing treaties and agreements with foreign countries.
II. Article 253 empowers only the State legislatures to make laws for implementing international treaties.
questions.explanation: Article 253 gives Parliament power to make any law for the whole or any part of India to implement any treaty, agreement or convention with another country. State legislatures do not hold this power under Article 253.

statements: 1. Agriculture is a subject in the State List of the Seventh Schedule.
2. Police is a subject in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule.
3. Public health and sanitation is a subject in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule.
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct. Agriculture is in the State List, while police and public health and sanitation are State List subjects, not Union List subjects.

statements: I. The WTO agreement entered into force on 1 January 1995.
II. The Marrakesh Agreement establishing the World Trade Organization was signed in Marrakesh, Morocco.
III. The WTO agreement was signed in Geneva, Switzerland.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct: the agreement was signed at Marrakesh on 15 April 1994 and took effect on 1 January 1995. Statement III is wrong because the signing took place in Marrakesh, not Geneva.
